messages:
Sam (AE): Kicking off OrcinPay POC — they want Redwood Private inside their AWS account (multi-AZ), strict egress-only allowlist, and preservation of client source IPs for downstream logging. Any blockers?
Mira (SE): High-level tradeoffs: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives isolation and simpler cross-account setup. VPC Peering (or TGW attachment) preserves src IP more naturally but requires route updates and CIDR non-overlap.
John (NetOps): Clarify: If traffic flows through their TGW/NAT, we must ensure they're not performing SNAT. Also check if their onprem VPN does hairpinning — that can rewrite src IPs.
Paula (OrcinPay Admin): Procurement wants to know if PrivateLink costs more and if HA across AZs changes price. Also they insist no egress except to Redwood control plane & S3 model fetch.
Mira (SE): PrivateLink has endpoint-hour and cross-AZ network costs on AWS; our quote includes a small setup surcharge compared to peering. Multi-AZ HA requires reserved capacity or dedicated nodes (monthly commit). I'll include a delta in the quote.
Anna (Security): Security Qs for questionnaire: where is TLS terminated? Do we support CMKs? Are logs containing secrets?
Liz (Eng): Recommended TLS termination is on the customer NLB for passthrough (keeps client IP). We support customer-managed CMKs for keys. Logs can contain prompt metadata — we'll provide redaction guidance and configurable retention windows.
John (NetOps): Firewall allowlist snippet for their ops team — concrete rules they can paste:
```
# egress from Redwood private nodes (customer VPC)
TCP 443 -> api.redwood-inference.com (control plane + model sync)
TCP 443 -> s3.amazonaws.com (model artifact fetch)
TCP 443 -> logs.redwood-inference.com (optional telemetry)
UDP 123 -> ntp.pool (time sync via NTP proxy)
TCP 22 -> bastion IPs (only if they request support access)
ICMP -> health checks (optional)
```
John (NetOps): Note for TGW: add routes for the Redwood subnet(s) and ensure TGW route table association allows spokes to reach the endpoint. If peering, create explicit route entries in the peered VPC route tables.
Paula (OrcinPay Admin): For PrivateLink, do we have to touch our route tables?
Mira (SE): No route edits for interface endpoints; just SG rules to allow inbound from the endpoint ENIs to your NLB/listener port. For peering/TGW, you must add routes and possibly allow cross-account route propagation.
Anna (Security): We'll need short, redacted answers for the RFP security questionnaire. Also confirm SOC2 coverage for Private deployments.
Liz (Eng): Private deployments are in our enterprise compliance scope; SOC2 artifacts available under NDA. I'll route the compliance pack to CS.
Sam (AE): Action items: Mira to deliver exact allowlist CIDRs + pricing delta; John to validate firewall snippet for TGW/peering; Liz to attach KMS/SOC2 pointer; Anna to draft short questionnaire answers.
Mira (SE): I'll post the allowlist + a 1-page runbook (PrivateLink vs Peering decision tree) by EOD. :thumbsup:
John (NetOps): Crucial gotcha: to preserve client-srcip through our infra, customers must use an NLB in TCP passthrough mode — ALBs that terminate TLS will break src IP unless X-Forwarded-For is injected and trusted.
Paula (OrcinPay Admin): Great, we'll confirm with our network team and share the NAT/TGW topology before tomorrow's tech call. Prefer 11am PST.
deploy-bot: Ticket created DEPL-4222 for orcinpay-private-poc; assignees: Mira, John.
Sam (AE): Thanks — I'll send calendar invite for 11am PST and cc procurement.
Paula (OrcinPay Admin): Thanks all.
